proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 e_{p,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
We first prove the concentration statement.  If \(Z\in[0,1]\) and
\(\psi(\lambda)=\log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\), exponential tilting gives
\(\psi''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)\).  Since every tilted
law is still supported on \([0,1]\),
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)
 \le E_{\lambda}\{(Z-1/2)^2\}\le\frac14.
\]
Together with \(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\), two integrations yield
\[
 \log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},
 \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes
\(\widehat p_x\) the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli variables
with common mean \(p_x\).  Exponential Markov inequality, (1), and
optimization at \(\lambda=4e_{p,n}\) give
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \bigl(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>e_{p,n}\bigr)
 \le 2e^{-2ne_{p,n}^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.                            \tag{2}
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le e_{p,n}\right)
 \ge1-\frac{\alpha}{3}.                                               \tag{3}
\]
The true mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one.  Hence, by
\(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\), the event in
(3) is exactly
\(\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\), and the
asserted coordinate bound is part of the same definition.

For the cell-count assertion, let \(N\) be binomial with parameters
\(n\) and \(p\).  For \(t>0\), exponential Markov inequality and
\(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\) imply
\[
 \Pr(N\le np/2)
 \le \exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log2\) makes the exponent
\(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\).  Since \(n_x\) is binomial with parameters
\(n\) and \(p_x\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) and a union
bound give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 &\le \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\\
 &\le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.                                           \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to bound mass profiling.  Let \(p=(p_x)\) and
\(p'=(p'_x)\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and fix
\(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) in every cell.
Put \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  The continuum constraints in
\(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\) give, for \(a\in I\),
\[
 f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2,
 \qquad |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)+e_n.
\]
The denominator is therefore strictly positive, and the definition
\(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\) yields
\[
 \left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                             \tag{5}
\]
Both mass vectors are within \(e_{p,n}\) of \(\widehat p\)
coordinatewise.  Thus (5) and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
 \right|
 \le2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}.                    \tag{6}
\]
Finally put \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>1\).  The tuning definitions in
\(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\) give
\(K_n\sim\log n/\log\log n\) and
\[
 b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{-\gamma})=O(r_n).
\]
Because \(m,\alpha,B_Y\) and all class radii are fixed,
\[
 \log\left(\frac{e_{p,n}}{r_n}\right)
 =-\frac12\log n+O(\log\log n)\longrightarrow-\infty.
\]
Consequently the right-hand side of (6) is \(o(r_n)\), as claimed.

Fix a sufficiently large \(n\).  We first establish the simultaneous
confidence event.  Conditional on the labels \((X_i)_{i=1}^n\), the
observations in every nonempty cell are independent and have the
conditional law given \(X=x\), by \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\).  Each real
and imaginary part of a probability-channel summand lies in \([-1,1]\).
The common-event structural response representation included in
\(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), together with
\(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), gives \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost surely;
hence each real and imaginary part of a marked-channel summand lies in
\([-B_Y,B_Y]\).

Apply the moment-generating-function calculation in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), after rescaling an interval
of length \(2c\), separately to the real and imaginary parts.  Since
\(|z|>u\) implies
\(\max\{|\operatorname{Re}z|,|\operatorname{Im}z|\}>u/\sqrt2\), when
\(n_x>\lambda_n\), for each \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\),
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|
 >2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\ \middle|\ (X_i)_{i=1}^n
 \right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n},                                         \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 \Pr\left(
 |\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-G_x(s,t)|
 >2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\ \middle|\ (X_i)_{i=1}^n
 \right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n}.                                         \tag{2}
\]
If \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the empirical-channel definitions, including
the empty-cell convention, and \(|F_x|\le1\), \(|G_x|\le B_Y\) show
deterministically that the same deviations are bounded by
\(\rho^F_{x,n}=2\) and \(\rho^G_{x,n}=2B_Y\).  A conditional union
bound over two channels, all cells, and all grid points therefore has
failure probability at most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6.                 \tag{3}
\]
Combining (3) with the mass-region failure probability \(\alpha/3\) from
\(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), and then integrating over
the labels, gives, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})
 \ge1-\alpha/3-\alpha/6\ge1-\alpha.                                \tag{4}
\]

Suppose now that \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) occurs.  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\) in each of the
finitely many cells and
\(\mathrm{lem{:}atomic\text{-}grid\text{-}embedding}\) to the two
error laws.  Define the proof-intermediate tuple
\[
 \bar\theta_n=
 \bigl((p_x,\widetilde f_{x,n},\widetilde q_{x,n})_{x\in\mathcal X},
       \bar\phi_{1,n},\bar\phi_{2,n}\bigr).
\]
Its mass vector belongs to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) by the event.  If
\((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), then \(s,t\in\Gamma_n\).  Characteristic
functions have modulus at most one.  Moreover,
\(|\widehat f_x(u)|\le1\), and
\(|\widehat q_x(u)|\le\int|q_x|\le B_Y\), because
\(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) and \(f_x\) is a density.  Uniform approximation on
the interval \(\mathcal A\), whose length is \(2B_A\), implies
\[
 |\widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(u)-\widehat f_x(u)|\le2B_Aa_{f,n},
 \qquad
 |\widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(u)-\widehat q_x(u)|\le2B_Aa_{q,n}.    \tag{5}
\]
Also, at grid points,
\[
 |\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)|
 \le|\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)-\phi_1(s)|
   +|\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-\phi_2(t)|
 \le2\tau_{e,n}.                                                     \tag{6}
\]
The already established factorization lemma, (5)--(6), and the triangle
inequality now give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|
 \widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(s+t)
 \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-F_x(s,t)
 \right|
 &\le2B_Aa_{f,n}+2\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^F_n,\\
 \left|
 \widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(s+t)
 \bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-G_x(s,t)
 \right|
 &\le2B_Aa_{q,n}+2B_Y\tau_{e,n}\le\delta^G_n.                      \tag{7}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Combining (7) with the empirical inequalities defining
\(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) verifies every residual constraint in
\(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\); the two embedding
lemmas verify every deterministic sieve constraint.  Hence
\[
 \bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}.                                  \tag{8}
\]
The quotient conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\), with the true
mass vector, then gives
\[
 \|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}.             \tag{9}
\]

Finally consider an arbitrary realized sample; no confidence event is
used in this last step.  Put \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  For any
\(\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), the simplex constraint, the marked
outer envelope, and the strict bound \(f_x\ge\kappa/2\) on \(I\) yield
\[
 |\mu_\theta(a)|
 \le\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x
 \left(B_Y+\frac{e_n}{f_x(a)}\right)
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                             \tag{10}
\]
If the feasible set is nonempty, put
\(\ell(a)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\) and
\(u(a)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\).  Equation
(10) and \(\ell(a)\le u(a)\) imply
\[
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le B_Y,
 \qquad -B_Y\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n},
 \qquad \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n}.                       \tag{11}
\]
Together with \(-B_Y\le B_Y\), these four pairwise inequalities show
\[
 \max\{-B_Y,\ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\}
 \le\min\{B_Y,u(a)+b_{\mu,n}\}.
\]
Both endpoints lie in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\).  If the feasible set is empty,
both endpoints equal zero by
\(\mathrm{def{:}profiled\text{-}band}\).  Therefore, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \qquad 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.                                            \tag{12}
\]
Equations (4), (8), (9), and (12) prove exactly the stated concentration,
outer-embedding, ADRF-approximation, and clipping conclusions.  No
inverse-diameter assertion is used or obtained.

Fix \(n\) at least as large as the common deterministic threshold in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).  We first
verify measurability and finiteness of the explicit construction.  At
this fixed \(n\), the deterministic signal families are compact.  Their
defining continuum inequalities are closed.  Moreover, the calculation
in \(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\) gives a
uniform \(L^1(\mathcal A)\) bound for every \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), and
the marked envelope gives one for every
\(q\in\mathscr Q_n(f)\).  Equivalence of norms in the fixed
finite-dimensional spline spaces therefore bounds their coefficient
vectors.  The error families are closed subsets of the product of a
finite simplex and \([-H_n,H_n]^{M_n}\), and the mass simplex is compact.
Thus all deterministic constraints define a fixed compact
coefficient--weight--atom set \(K\).  The lower constraint
\(f_x\ge\kappa/2\) on \(I\) ensures that every quotient used below has
a strictly positive denominator.

For a realized sample \(z\), let \(h(z,\theta)\) be the maximum of zero
and the positive parts of the finitely many sample-dependent mass and
channel constraint violations in
\(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\), with all
deterministic constraints absorbed into \(K\).  Then
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)=\{\theta\in K:h(z,\theta)=0\}.                 \tag{1}
\]
The map \(h\) is measurable in \(z\) and continuous in \(\theta\): the
empirical transforms are measurable, and every fitted transform is a
finite continuous function of coefficients, weights, and atom
locations.  The map \((a,\theta)\mapsto\mu_\theta(a)\) is continuous on
\(I\times K\), by the spline formulas and the denominator bound.

We give a direct measurable-extrema argument.  Let \(K_0\) be a
countable dense subset of \(K\), and define
\[
 d(z)=\inf_{\theta\in K}h(z,\theta),
 \qquad
 V_k^+(z,a)=\sup_{\theta\in K}
 \{\mu_\theta(a)-kh(z,\theta)\},
\]
with \(V_k^-\) defined by replacing \(\mu_\theta\) by
\(-\mu_\theta\).  Continuity in \(\theta\) permits every displayed
infimum and supremum to be taken over \(K_0\).  Hence
\(d,V_k^+,V_k^-\) are jointly measurable in their displayed arguments.
Compactness shows that \(d(z)=0\) exactly when
\(\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)\ne\varnothing\).  On this event,
\[
 V_k^+(z,a)\downarrow
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a),
 \qquad
 V_k^-(z,a)\downarrow
 -\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a).                \tag{2}
\]
To prove the first limit, take maximizers in \(K\).  A feasible point
gives a fixed finite lower bound on the penalized objective, while
\(\mu_\theta(a)\) is bounded on compact \(K\); hence the violations of
the maximizers tend to zero.  Every convergent subsequence therefore has
a feasible limit, whose objective is at most the feasible supremum.  The
reverse inequality holds because feasible points pay zero penalty.  The
second limit is the same argument applied to \(-\mu_\theta\).

Equation (2), the measurable event \(\{d=0\}\), and the stipulated zero
value on \(\{d>0\}\) prove joint sample-and-index measurability of the
profiled extrema.  Maxima and minima with the constants \(\pm B_Y\)
preserve measurability.  For each sample the extrema are continuous in
\(a\) by the same compactness argument, so the supremum defining \(W_n\)
may be taken over a fixed countable dense subset of the compact interval
\(I\) and is measurable.  Equation (10) of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) proves
finiteness, and its clipping conclusion proves, for every sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad(a\in I),
 \qquad0\le W_n\le2B_Y.                                              \tag{3}
\]

Let \(P\in\mathcal M\).  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the stability
lemma provides \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) satisfying
\(|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-\mu(a)|\le b_{\mu,n}\) simultaneously for
all \(a\in I\).  The structural response-surface bound included in
\(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\) gives
\(-B_Y\le\mu(a)=E_P[Y(a)]\le B_Y\).  Therefore, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le\mu(a),                                                         \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge\mu(a).                                                         \tag{5}
\]
In (4), both the raw lower expression and \(-B_Y\) are at most
\(\mu(a)\); in (5), both the raw upper expression and \(B_Y\) are at
least \(\mu(a)\).  The clipping rule thus preserves both inequalities,
and
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\subseteq
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.             \tag{6}
\]
Taking probabilities in (6) and using the uniform event bound in the
stability lemma gives
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}
 \ge1-\alpha.                                                        \tag{7}
\]
Joint measurability, (3), and (7) verify every condition in
\(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\), so
\(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  Finally, (3) and
monotonicity of expectation give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le2B_Y.
\]
This argument proves honesty and clipping only; it invokes no shrinking
inverse-diameter bound.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and a sufficiently large
\(n\).  Define the clipped error
\[
 U_j^{H}=\max\{-H_n,\min\{U_j,H_n\}\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\) and the pointwise
bound
\(\mathbf 1\{|U_j|>H_n\}\le |U_j|^{q_e}H_n^{-q_e}\) give
\[
 P(|U_j|>H_n)\le M_eH_n^{-q_e}.
\]
Consequently, for every real \(t\),
\[
 \left|E_Pe^{itU_j^H}-\phi_j(t)\right|
 \le2P(|U_j|>H_n)
 \le2M_eH_n^{-q_e}=\tau_{e,n},                                      \tag{1}
\]
and clipping also gives
\[
 E_P|U_j^H|^{q_e}\le E_P|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e.                         \tag{2}
\]
For \(j=2\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) and
\(|U_2-U_2^H|\le |U_2|\mathbf 1\{|U_2|>H_n\}\) yield
\[
 |E_PU_2^H|
 =|E_P(U_2^H-U_2)|
 \le E_P\{|U_2|\mathbf 1(|U_2|>H_n)\}
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                                 \tag{3}
\]

We next replace the law of \(U_j^H\), whose support is the compact
interval \([-H_n,H_n]\), by a finite atomic law while preserving every
quantity needed on the grid.  Put \(D=2|\Gamma_n|+2\), and define the
continuous map
\[
 v(u)=\bigl((\operatorname{Re}e^{itu},\operatorname{Im}e^{itu})_
 {t\in\Gamma_n},u,|u|^{q_e}\bigr)\in\mathbb R^D.
\]
The vector \(E_Pv(U_j^H)\) belongs to the convex hull of the compact set
\(v([-H_n,H_n])\): finite simple-function approximations to the integral
belong to that convex hull, and a convex hull of a compact subset of the
finite-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^D\) is compact.

Here is a direct finite-support reduction.  If a convex representation
uses more than \(D+1\) points, the corresponding augmented vectors
\((1,v(u_r))\in\mathbb R^{D+1}\) are linearly dependent.  Hence there
are coefficients \(a_r\), not all zero, satisfying
\(\sum_ra_r=0\) and \(\sum_ra_rv(u_r)=0\).  After changing the common
sign if necessary, some \(a_r>0\).  Subtracting
\(c(a_r)_r\) from the weights, with
\(c=\min_{a_r>0}w_r/a_r\), preserves their sum and barycenter, keeps all
weights nonnegative, and makes at least one weight zero.  Iteration leaves
at most
\[
 D+1=2|\Gamma_n|+3\le M_n
\]
atoms.  Padding with zero-weight atoms at \(H_n\) and ordering the atom
locations produces an atomic characteristic function
\(\bar\phi_{j,n}\) which agrees with \(E_Pe^{itU_j^H}\) at every
\(t\in\Gamma_n\), has the same mean, has support in \([-H_n,H_n]\), and
has the same \(q_e\)-moment.  Equations (1)--(3) therefore give
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|\le\tau_{e,n},       \tag{4}
\]
and, when \(j=2\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                                 \tag{5}
\]

It remains to verify the continuum protected-frequency condition in
\(\mathrm{def{:}error\text{-}sieves}\).  Let
\(\Delta_n=(B_AK_n)^{-1}\), the spacing of \(\Gamma_n\).  Since
\(K_n\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\) one has
\(T_n\ge\nu_0\), and each \(|t|\le\nu_0\) has a
\(\gamma\in\Gamma_n\) with \(|t-\gamma|\le\Delta_n/2\).
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\), (2), and Lyapunov's
inequality give
\[
 E_P|U_j|\le M_e^{1/q_e},
 \qquad \sum_{\ell}w_{j\ell}|u_{j\ell}|\le M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
Using \(|e^{itu}-e^{i\gamma u}|\le|t-\gamma||u|\), the equality of the
atomic and clipped transforms at \(\gamma\), (1), and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}modulus}\), we obtain
\[
 |\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)|
 \ge c_0-\tau_{e,n}-M_e^{1/q_e}\Delta_n.                             \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, the two Lipschitz changes from \(t\) to \(\gamma\) each cost at
most \(M_e^{1/q_e}\Delta_n/2\).

The grid definitions give \(|\mathcal D_n|=O(K_n^4)\), so
\(\lambda_n=O(\log K_n)\), \(n/\lambda_n\to\infty\),
\(H_n\to\infty\), and \(\Delta_n\to0\).  Hence the last two terms in
(6) sum to at most \(c_0/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The
atomic law obeys the support and moment constraints by construction, so
\(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\widetilde\Phi_{j,n}\).  For \(j=2\), (5) is even
stronger than the additional bound
\(2M_eH_n^{1-q_e}\) defining \(\Phi_{2,n}\).  Thus
\(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\Phi_{j,n}\), and (4)--(5) prove the result.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).  By the defining
Jackson approximation property of the constant
\(C_{\beta,\mathcal A}\), the order choice
\(d=\lceil\beta\rceil+1\), assumptions
\(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and the definitions in
\(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\), there are splines
\(\widetilde f_{x,n}\) and \(\widetilde q_{x,n}\) in the stated
order-\(d\) spline space such that
\[
 \|\widetilde f_{x,n}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{f,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde q_{x,n}-q_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{q,n}.       \tag{1}
\]
Because \(K_n\to\infty\) and \(\beta>3/2\), one has
\(a_{f,n}\to0\); in particular, \(a_{f,n}<\kappa/2\) for every
sufficiently large \(n\).

The function \(f_x\) is nonnegative and integrates to one over
\(\mathcal A\), by its definition as the conditional density and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\).  Thus (1) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}denominator}\) give
\[
 \widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\ge-a_{f,n}\quad(a\in\mathcal A),
 \qquad
 \widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\ge\kappa-a_{f,n}\ge\kappa/2\quad(a\in I),     \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\,da-1\right|
 \le\int_{\mathcal A}|\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-f_x(a)|\,da
 \le2B_Aa_{f,n}.                                                     \tag{3}
\]

We also need the marked envelope.  The common-event representation in
\(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), which is
part of \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) imply \(|Y|\le B_Y\) almost surely.
Conditional Jensen inequality therefore gives
\(|m_x(a)|\le B_Y\) for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\).  Hence
\(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) almost everywhere by \(q_x=m_xf_x\).  Since
\(\beta>3/2\), the Sobolev representatives of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) are
continuous on \(\mathbb R\); the almost-everywhere inequality therefore
extends to every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  Using (1),
\[
 |\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)|
 \le |q_x(a)|+a_{q,n}
 \le B_Y\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)+a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n},
 \qquad a\in\mathcal A.                                             \tag{4}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) are exactly the relaxed outer constraints in
\(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\).  They prove
\(\widetilde f_{x,n}\in\mathscr F_n\) and
\(\widetilde q_{x,n}\in\mathscr Q_n(\widetilde f_{x,n})\).

For completeness, the relaxed families are compact at every fixed
\(n\).  Their continuum inequalities are closed in the finite-dimensional
spline space.  If \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), then, writing
\(f_- = \max\{-f,0\}\),
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}|f|
 =\int_{\mathcal A}f+2\int_{\mathcal A}f_-
 \le1+6B_Aa_{f,n},                                                   \tag{5}
\]
because \(f_-\le a_{f,n}\) and
\(|\int_{\mathcal A}f-1|\le2B_Aa_{f,n}\).  The marked envelope then
uniformly bounds \(\int_{\mathcal A}|q|\).  Norm equivalence in each
fixed finite-dimensional spline space bounds all coefficients.  Thus
the two closed families are bounded and hence compact.  No positivity or
exact-density constraint beyond the displayed outer constraints is used.

It remains to compare the profiled quotient with the causal target.
The already established \(\mathrm{thm{:}adrf\text{-}id}\) gives
\(\mu(a)=\sum_xp_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\) on \(I\).  For \(a\in I\), (1)--(2),
\(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\), and \(|q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
       -\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 &\le\frac{|\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)-q_x(a)|}
 {\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
 +\frac{|q_x(a)|\,|\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-f_x(a)|}
 {f_x(a)\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}\\
 &\le\frac{a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}}{\kappa-a_{f,n}}\\
 &\le2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}).                              \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The nonnegative masses \(p_x\) sum to one, so summing (6) proves
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x
 \frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}-\mu(a)
 \right|
 \le2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})
 \le b_{\mu,n},
\]
where the last inequality is the definition in
\(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\).
